summary: Joseph Loizzo works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. He studied at Amherst College, Harvard University, and under Robert A. F. Thurman, founded the Nalanda Institute for Contemplative Science, and was a Visiting Scholar of Religion at Columbia University in 2007.

Joseph M. Kitagawa (1915–1992) was a scholar of religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Rikkyo, CDSP, Seabury-Western, and Chicago under Joachim Wach, later serving as professor and Divinity School Dean at Chicago (1951–1987).
Joseph Margolis (1924–2021) was a philosopher who earned his M.A. from Columbia University (~1947–1950). He held the Laura H. Carnell Chair of Philosophy at Temple University in 1991.

Joseph Marino works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Washington (attested 2013–2017), where he studied under doctoral supervisor Richard Salomon and teacher Collett Cox.

Joseph Needham (1900–1995) worked in Sinology and history/archaeology. Educated at Oundle and Cambridge, he was a Fellow (~1924–1995) and Master (~1966–1976) of Gonville and Caius College, Cambridge Reader in Biochemistry (~1933–1966), and Director of Needham Research Institute (~1987–1990).

Joseph Prabhu is a scholar in philosophy and religious studies who studied under Bernard Williams. His posts include Associate Professor of Philosophy at California State University, Los Angeles (attested 1989, 2007), alongside visiting professorships at UCSB, UTC Bangalore, and Bossey.

Joseph Ratzinger (1927–2022) was a religious studies scholar and philosopher who studied at the University of Munich and Ducal Georgianum. He held academic posts at Munich (1958–1959), Bonn (1959–1963), Münster (1963–1966), Tübingen (1966–1969), and Regensburg (1969–1977).

Joseph Rock (1884–1962) was a scholar in Sinology and Tibetology. He taught at the Mid-Pacific Institute (1908), served as curator and official botanist at the University of Hawaiʻi (1908, 1911–1920), and was an explorer for the USDA (~1920–1924).

Joseph Tiefenthaler (1710–1785) was a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He served as a Jesuit missionary in the Society of Jesus from 1729 to 1773 and was Rector of St. Peter's College, Agra.

Joseph Toussaint Reinaud (1795–1867) worked in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy, held posts at the Bibliothèque nationale de France (from 1824) and INALCO (1838), and served as president of Société Asiatique.

Joseph Vendryes (1875–1960) was a linguist who studied at the Faculty of Arts of Paris under Antoine Meillet. He held posts at the University of Paris (~1907–1946), EPHE (~1907–1950), and École Normale Supérieure (~1923–1938).

Joseph Walser is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied under Isshi Yamada, Adolf von Wuertenburg, and David S. Pacini, and held an academic post at Loyola University Chicago (attested 1998).

Joseph von Hammer-Purgstall (1774–1856) was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at the K.k. Akademie für Orientalische Sprachen (~1789–1799) and held a post at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (~1847–1849).
Josho Nozawa (1906–1968) worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied under Susumu Yamaguchi and served as a professor at Koyasan University (attested 1950).
Joshua Marshman (1768–1837) worked in Indology and Sinology. He studied at Bristol Baptist College (~1794–1799) and under Johannes Lassar (~1805–1810), and founded Serampore College in 1818.

Joshua T. Katz (1969–) is a linguist who studied at Yale, Oxford, and Harvard. He was Cotsen Professor in the Humanities at Princeton University (1998–2022) and became a Senior Fellow at the American Enterprise Institute in ~2022.
Joshua W. C. Cutler works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Ngawang Wangyal and held a post at the Tibetan Buddhist Learning Center (attested 2004).

Josiah Royce (1855–1916) was an American philosopher. He studied at the University of California, Berkeley, under Hermann Lotze at Göttingen, and at Johns Hopkins, before holding posts at UC Berkeley (~1878–1882) and Harvard University (1882–1916).

Jost Gippert (1956–) is a scholar in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Marburg (~1972–1973) and served as Director of the Institute for Empirical Linguistics at Goethe University Frankfurt (1994–2022).

José Ignacio Cabezón (1956–) specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. Educated at Caltech, Sera Jey, and Wisconsin under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, he held posts at Iliff School of Theology (~1989–2001) and UC Santa Barbara (from 2001).
